subject.title: fix(cron): support current and session: targets in initial delivery resolution

question: Should typed cron create and replacement persist explicit announce delivery for `current` and `session:` output jobs, matching raw normalization and runtime planning?
rationale: Source and proof support the alignment, but only the cron owner can confirm that no supported consumer intentionally relies on omitted delivery remaining distinct from explicit announce in the serialized job shape.

options.title: Accept canonical alignment
options.body: Merge the patch because it makes typed creation persist the same default already established by normalization and execution.

options.title: Preserve omitted representation
options.body: Pause and document the concrete supported consumer that requires omitted delivery to remain distinct, then adjust sibling paths to preserve that contract consistently.

recommendation.title: Accept canonical alignment
recommendation.body: Merge the patch because it makes typed creation persist the same default already established by normalization and execution.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced and merged the persistent-session product contract that this delivery-default alignment follows.
